description: Verification check tiers, their fixed ordering, and which tiers each risk level requires. JSON content under a .yaml extension, matching capabilities.yaml and routes.yaml (design 4.4). Consumed by src/runtime/verification/engine.js.

notes: A tier whose command could not be detected and was not explicitly declared absent resolves to UNRESOLVED, and an UNRESOLVED required tier forces the whole report to INCONCLUSIVE. A gate never answers PASS about a check it did not run.
modelReviewIsPrimaryProof is false and is validated as false at load: a model-based tier may lower a verdict to FAIL but can never establish PASS on its own.

Each tier declares the recovery failureClass its failure means. A tier declaration is structural evidence and outranks the keyword classifier reading an error string, the same precedence recovery.js already applies between check names and error prose.

unresolvedDetectionFailureClass is CONTEXT_MISSING rather than ENVIRONMENT_FAILURE: what is missing is knowledge of the command, and the targeted action is to find it or declare it in plan.md, not to diagnose the machine.

tiers.name: Parse
tiers.description: Syntax-only check of the changed sources. Cheapest possible evidence that the edit is even well-formed.

tiers.name: Build
tiers.description: Compile or bundle the project. A broken build makes every later result a description of the broken build rather than of the change, which is why it is fatal.

tiers.name: Static analysis
tiers.description: Type checking and linting. Deterministic, no test fixtures required, and finds whole classes of defect before a single test runs.

tiers.name: Targeted tests
tiers.description: Tests scoped to the change. Falls back to the broad test command when no target pattern is available, and the report records that it did.

tiers.name: Broad tests
tiers.description: The full suite. Required from MEDIUM risk upward — this is the tier the risk scaling actually turns on.

tiers.name: Structural invariants
tiers.description: Repository-shape checks the caller supplies — guard suites, architecture fitness functions, layering rules. Not derivable from a manifest, so the compiler asks for them.

tiers.name: Requirement satisfaction
tiers.description: One check per requirement the change claims to satisfy. A requirement with no executable check is reported unevaluated, never satisfied — an assertion is not a verification.

tiers.name: Change scope
tiers.description: Compares the files actually touched against the bound the contract declared before implementation. Catches the change that passed every test by also rewriting things nobody asked for.

tiers.name: Model-based review
tiers.description: Runs last, after every deterministic tier has already produced its evidence. Advisory by construction: it can lower a verdict to FAIL but can never establish PASS (FR-009).

LOW.description: Isolated, reversible change. Deterministic tiers plus tests scoped to the edit.

MEDIUM.description: Default. Adds the full suite, because a change of this size can break something it never mentions.

HIGH.description: Security, auth, payments, data migration. Adds structural and requirement evidence, and tightens the retry bound because repeated blind attempts are themselves a risk.

CRITICAL.description: Production outage, breaking change, data loss. Every tier including a recorded model review; one retry, then a human decides.
